body: A converter is a purpose-built device — a hardware circuit, integrated chip, or firmware/software artifact — whose sole function is transforming a signal or quantity from one representational domain to another while preserving the carried information content across the transfer. Parameters: (1) input domain — the representational form of the incoming signal (e.g., continuous-time analog voltage, discrete digital codes, a given sampling rate); (2) output domain — the representational form produced (e.g., discrete digital codes, continuous-time analog voltage, a different sampling rate); (3) transfer law — the reproducible mapping relating input to output (sampling plus quantization, a quantization ladder plus reconstruction filter, a resampling kernel with interpolation and anti-imaging/anti-aliasing filtering, level or impedance transformation); (4) fidelity constraints — the bounds within which content is preserved (bandwidth, bit depth, jitter, error bound). Persistence mechanism: fabricated as silicon circuits or packaged as firmware and software libraries, distributed through electronics and software supply chains, maintained by the engineering discipline of signal processing, and replaced when the transfer law or fidelity target changes. [formal: conversor | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

Fisher information is a human-made measure, for a parametric statistical model, of how much information an observable random variable X (or a sample of it) carries about an unknown parameter θ governing its distribution; it is defined as the expected squared score, I(θ) = E[(∂/∂θ log p(X|θ))²], equivalently — under regularity conditions — the negative expected second derivative of the log-likelihood, I(θ) = −E[∂²/∂θ² log p(X|θ)]. Parameters: the parametric family of distributions p(x|θ), the parameter θ (scalar, or a vector θ giving the Fisher information matrix), and the sampling scheme (independent samples make the information additive: nI(θ) for n iid observations). Identifying properties: non-negative; equal to the variance of the score under regularity; in the scalar case it is the reciprocal of the minimum variance of unbiased estimators, and in general it anchors the Cramér-Rao bound on estimator variance; it transforms by the Jacobian under one-to-one reparameterization. It persists as a named quantity in mathematical statistics — maintained in textbooks, implemented in maximum-likelihood estimation and in information geometry, where it defines the Fisher-Rao metric on the space of probability distributions. [formal: mathematical | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.08]

Regression diagnostic is a human-made analytical procedure that examines the residuals, influence, and specification errors of a fitted regression model to assess its reliability. Parameters: (1) residual pattern, (2) influence measures, (3) specification tests. Persistence: textbooks, software routines, peer-review norms. [formal: diagnostica regressionis | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.04]

Truth is the human-authored map of the conditions under which a statement is held to be correct, stable, or binding. It carves its territory by parameters of correspondence versus coherence versus pragmatic utility, the domain of application, and the social mechanisms of validation. Its boundaries shift with epistemic communities — science, law, everyday conversation — and the map persists through language, argument, institutional certification, and the practice of correction, not through a natural property of propositions. [formal: veritas | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.45]

Spectral flanger is a human-made audio effect technique that produces the flanger's characteristic moving comb-filter notches by realizing the flanging delay in the frequency domain instead of as a time-domain delay line. Mechanism: the input is decomposed into a time-frequency representation (typically the STFT); a short, slowly modulated spectral delay is applied as a time-varying linear phase ramp (or equivalent per-bin phase/gain modulation) across the bins; the delayed and undelayed representations are summed and resynthesized, so notches sweep the spectrum at the modulation rate. Parameters: (1) modulation depth of the spectral delay (up to roughly 15 ms worth of phase); (2) LFO modulation rate (typically 0.01-10 Hz); (3) wet/dry mix ratio; (4) optional comb feedback; (5) analysis window and hop. It is distinct from the classic delay-line flanger (a sample-accurate time shift mixed with the dry signal) and from time-stretching (which rescales the whole spectrum rather than modulating a narrowband delay). Persistence mechanism: the technique is fixed by its algorithmic recipe (spectral decomposition, modulated per-bin delay, summation, resynthesis) and persists as reusable DSP code and effect-design documentation in audio-effect toolkits and research implementations. [formal: spectral-flanger | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

state-space-model is a human-made mathematical framework for representing the evolution of a system's internal state over time using a set of first-order differential or difference equations. It expresses the system through state variables (capturing all relevant internal information), input variables (external influences), and output equations (observable quantities). Parameters: state dimension, linearity (linear vs. nonlinear), time domain (continuous vs. discrete), observability and controllability properties. Persistence mechanism: maintained as a formal representation in control theory, system dynamics, signal processing, and estimation theory, instantiated through equations and numerical solvers. [formal: state-space-model | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A wah-wah is a human-made audio effect technique that sweeps the center frequency of a bandpass filter over time, producing a vocal-like 'wah' sound. Mechanism: the input signal passes through a bandpass filter whose center frequency is modulated by a low-frequency oscillator (LFO) or expression pedal, typically sweeping between ~200 Hz and ~2 kHz. The sweep depth, rate, and Q (bandwidth) of the filter define the effect's character. Parameters: (1) center frequency range (typically 200 Hz–2 kHz); (2) sweep rate (LFO-controlled, ~0.1–5 Hz, or expression-pedal controlled by the player); (3) filter Q (bandwidth — wider Q yields a broader, less pronounced sweep); (4) sweep depth (how far the center frequency moves). Persistence mechanism: the technique is fixed by its signal chain (bandpass filter with sweepable center frequency) and persists as hardware guitar pedals (the classic Vox wah-wah circuit), DSP plugins, synthesizer filter envelopes, and built-in patches on multi-effects units. [formal: wah-wah | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Regression is a human-made family of statistical estimation methods that fit a mathematical model to observed data to quantify the relationship between a dependent (outcome) variable and one or more independent (predictor) variables, yielding fitted parameters usable for prediction and inference. Parameters: (1) model form — linear, polynomial, generalized (e.g., logistic), or nonlinear; (2) estimation criterion — ordinary least squares, maximum likelihood, or regularized variants (ridge, lasso); (3) data layout — the outcome variable, the predictor variables, and the sample; (4) the working assumptions the fit makes about the error structure, which the method estimates rather than verifies. Regression is thereby distinguished from its diagnostic machinery: it produces the fitted model and its parameters, while residual analysis and influence measures are tools applied afterwards to evaluate the fit. Its persistence mechanism is teaching and re-implementation: textbooks, statistical software, and every predictive or inferential task re-instantiate the family for each new analyst; the forms extend whenever a new criterion or model family is added. [formal: regressio quantitatis | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.25]

An envelope follower is a circuit or algorithm that tracks the slowly varying amplitude of an input signal — its envelope — and outputs that amplitude as a separate, usable control signal without altering the input. Parameters: (1) detection — conversion of instantaneous signal level into a unipolar level (precision rectification, squaring, or magnitude computation); (2) time constants — attack (rise) and release (fall) smoothing that decide which level variations are tracked and which are averaged out; (3) output form — a voltage, digital value, or control signal with a defined gain relation to the measured level. The follower is a derivation stage: it produces a second signal about the first. Persistence mechanism: realized as an analog block (precision rectifier followed by RC low-pass smoothing) and a digital block (one-pole smoothing on rectified magnitude), standardized as the level-detection primitive in every automatic gain control, compressor, limiter, sidechain processor, and peak meter; the pattern persists through circuit-design textbooks and DSP code libraries that reproduce the rectify–smooth structure across generations of hardware and software. [formal: secutor | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Spectral processing is the method of analyzing and manipulating signals in their frequency-domain representation. It operates by applying the Fourier transform (or variants like STFT, DCT, wavelet transforms) to decompose a time-domain waveform into its constituent frequency components, then applying operations (filtering, amplification, attenuation, phase manipulation) to those frequency bands before reconstructing a modified signal via inverse transform. Parameters: (1) the transform type (DFT, FFT, STFT, wavelet), (2) the window function for time-localized transforms, (3) the frequency resolution determined by transform size and sampling rate, (4) the specific manipulation applied to spectral components. Persistence mechanism: implemented in DSP algorithms, embedded in audio software (spectral editors, FFT analyzers, spectral plugins), taught in signal processing curricula. [formal: spectrale_proc | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

Presumption-of-innocence is a human-made legal principle that structures criminal proceedings by requiring the state to prove guilt rather than the accused to prove innocence. Its parameters are: (1) the accused enters proceedings with legal innocence assigned, (2) the prosecution bears the full burden of proving each element of the charged offense, (3) the accused need not present any defense or evidence, (4) any reasonable doubt in the prosecution's case mandates acquittal. Its persistence mechanism is constitutional entrenchment and statutory criminal procedure codes in jurisdictions that adopt the principle, enforced through appellate review of trial-level errors. [formal: praesumptio innocentiae | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.91]

Variational inference is an approximation method for Bayesian inference that recasts posterior computation as optimization: it fixes a tractable family of distributions (the variational family, e.g. factorized Gaussians) and finds the member q* minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence KL(q || p) to the true posterior, equivalently maximizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO) = E_q[ln p(x,z)] - E_q[ln q(z)]. Its parameters are the variational family (the support and factorization assumed for q), the recognition parameters (the variational parameters of q, such as means and covariances), and the optimization procedure (coordinate ascent, stochastic gradient descent on the ELBO, or amortization through a neural network). It persists because the ELBO is a computable objective that makes posterior approximation scalable to models where exact or MCMC inference is intractable; it is taught as one of the standard classes of approximate Bayesian methods and implemented in probabilistic programming and deep generative models (variational autoencoders). [formal: inferentia variationalis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

minimum-phase-filter is a human-made filter class defined by the property that its phase response is the minimum possible for its magnitude response, equivalently having all zeros and poles inside the unit circle for discrete-time or in left half-plane for continuous-time, causal and stable. Parameters are filter order, magnitude response specification, zero/pole locations, and implementation type. It persists through formal DSP theory, textbook codification, and repeated implementation in audio processing libraries and hardware designs. [formal: filter | substrate: matter | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.14]

Falsifiability is a human-made epistemological criterion that demarcates scientific claims from non-scientific ones by requiring that every scientific theory admit of at least one conceivable observation that could count against it. Parameters: (1) the theory or hypothesis being evaluated, (2) the set of possible observations that would contradict it, (3) the observational or experimental framework within which contradiction is determinable. Persistence mechanism: persists through philosophy of science textbooks (Popper, Lakatos, Kuhn), scientific methodology courses, peer-review standards that implicitly apply falsification reasoning, and institutional research funding criteria that require falsifiable proposals. [formal: falsabilitas | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An f-divergence is a human-made class of statistical divergences parameterized by a convex function f. For two probability distributions P, Q on the same measurable space, D_f[P||Q] = E_Q[f(dP/dQ)] where f is strictly convex with f(1)=0 and dP/dQ is the Radon-Nikodym derivative; specific choices of f produce specific divergences — f(t)=t log t yields KL-divergence, f(t)=(sqrt(t)-1)^2 yields Hellinger distance, f(t)=(t-1)^2 yields chi-squared divergence. Its parameters are the convex generator function f (determining which member of the family), the distribution pair (P,Q), and the measure-theoretic domain (absolute continuity of P w.r.t. Q required for the Radon-Nikodym derivative to exist). All members share the data-processing inequality: applying any stochastic map T monotonically decreases the divergence, D_f[P∘T^-1||Q∘T^-1] ≤ D_f[P||Q]. It persists as a unifying framework in information theory, statistics, and machine learning — enabling shared proofs of convexity, continuity, and convergence properties across the entire family — implemented in computational libraries, taught in information-theory curricula, and used to select divergence measures for specific applications (robustness, sensitivity, computational tractability). [formal: divergentia-f | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.11]

A sample-clock is a human-made timing reference that establishes a periodic grid marking the position of every audio sample in digital audio. It persists as a fixed sampling rate (e.g., 44.1 kHz, 48 kHz, 96 kHz) — the number of samples per second — which all digital audio hardware and software must agree on for correct playback and recording. Parameters: (1) sampling rate — the periodicity of the clock, expressed in samples per second; (2) clock source — the physical oscillator, crystal, or PLL that generates the timing pulses; (3) word length — the bit depth defining quantization, independent of but synchronized to the sample-clock. The mechanism of persistence: the sampling rate is encoded in audio file formats (WAV, AIFF, FLAC), specified in hardware specifications (audio interfaces, DACs, ADCs), and enforced by DSP implementations that process exactly N samples per second. [formal: exemplar-clock | substrate: matter | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Silence is a conceptual category marking the absence or suppression of sound, speech, or communication within a defined context. Its parameters are the domain (acoustic, discursive, legal, or social) and the agent (intentional or circumstantial). It persists through cultural conventions, legal statutes (e.g., right to silence), and social norms that define when quiet is meaningful versus merely absent. [formal: silentium | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A transducer is an engineered device that converts energy from one physical form to another through a defined transduction mechanism. Its parameters are: (1) an input domain specifying the source energy type (electrical, mechanical, thermal, optical, chemical, magnetic), (2) an output domain specifying the destination energy type, (3) a transduction principle governing the conversion (electromagnetic induction, piezoelectric effect, thermoelectric effect, photoelectric effect, electrostatic force), and (4) a linearity specification describing whether the output is proportional to the input. The transducer persists as a manufactured artifact, maintained through material integrity and calibration; its functional persistence depends on the continuity of the transduction medium and the stability of its conversion characteristics over time and operating range. [formal: transducer | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.42]

Vibrato is an audio effect that produces a slow, periodic variation in the pitch (frequency) of a sound signal, creating a wavering or throbbing quality. The mechanism uses a low-frequency oscillator — classically a sine wave at 4-8 Hz — to modulate the frequency of the sound source: in a synthesizer the LFO output is summed into the pitch input of the voltage-controlled oscillator, shifting its instantaneous frequency by the depth amount; in digital plugins the same LFO modulates the playback rate or phase accumulator of the source. Parameters: rate (LFO frequency, conventionally 4-8 Hz — slow enough to read as vibrato rather than trill or wobble), depth (peak pitch deviation, typically a few cents up to about a semitone), and waveform shape (sine for the classic smooth vibrato, triangle/square for harder character). Persistence mechanism: the pitch-LFO section of analog and digital synthesizers, vibrato circuits and effects in guitar amplifiers and pedals, DSP implementations in studio software (VST, AU, AAX plugins), and built-in effects in keyboards and vocal processors; specified in synthesis engineering documentation. Note on the name: many vintage guitar-amplifier controls labeled 'vibrato' in fact implement tremolo (periodic AMPLITUDE variation) — a historical misnomer carried over from stringed-instrument practice; this entry covers true pitch modulation, which is what the LFO definition's 'pitch (vibrato)' sense names. [formal: vibratio artificialis | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

test-entry-xyz is a placeholder entry created during a test shift to validate the entry filing workflow. It is a made record with no taxonomic content, existing solely to confirm that entries can be filed and retrieved without error. Parameters: (1) test-purpose — used only for pipeline validation; (2) ephemeral lifecycle — created for a shift, not intended for persistent classification; (3) minimal content — name and scope only, no substantive definition. It persists as a record in the Web of Corporata as long as the test entry remains in the graph. [formal: test | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.00]

A mixer is an audio processing device that accepts multiple input signals, allows independent level adjustment and routing of each channel, and produces a combined output (stereo or multi-channel). Its parameters include: number of input channels, number of bus outputs, signal path topology (analog through op-amp circuits or digital through DSP processing), channel strip features (EQ, gating, compression per channel), and monitoring capabilities. The device persists as physical hardware with knobs, faders, displays, and connections, or as software implementing the same functional architecture. Mixers operate by summing signals through additive or matrix-based routing while preserving each channel's adjustability. [formal: miscere | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Priming is the human-made conceptual framework describing the unconscious, non-deliberate activation of specific associations in memory that subsequently influences perception, cognition, and behavior. PARAMETERS: (1) the prime — an explicitly or implicitly presented stimulus (word, image, concept, context) that activates an association, (2) the target — the subsequent stimulus or task affected by the activated association, (3) the interval — the time between prime and target, typically milliseconds to minutes, (4) the match — the semantic, perceptual, or feature overlap between prime and target. PERSISTENCE: priming persists through repeated demonstration in experimental paradigms — semantic priming (cats activates dog), repetition priming (prior exposure speeds recognition), affective priming (prior emotion affects judgment), and procedural priming (prior action facilitates execution). The concept persists as a theoretical construct in cognitive psychology and neuroscience, operationalized through reaction-time measures, priming thresholds, and neural activation patterns. It is distinguished from memory retrieval (conscious recall), learning (stable performance change), and expectation (deliberate prediction). [formal: priming | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Conditional entropy is a human-made measure of remaining uncertainty in a random variable Y given knowledge of another random variable X. For discrete variables, H(Y|X) = -∑_x∑_y p(x,y) log p(y|x) = ∑_x p(x) H(Y|X=x). It extends Shannon entropy to the setting of dependent variables and satisfies the chain rule H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X). The measure is always non-negative and equals H(Y) when X and Y are independent. Conditional entropy persists through its role in defining mutual information (I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X)), channel capacity, and conditional independence structures in graphical models. [formal: conditional-entropy | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Memory consolidation is a human-made conceptual model that maps the natural process by which initially labile memories are stabilized into long-lasting storage. Parameters: (1) synaptic consolidation — cellular mechanisms (protein synthesis, AMPA receptor insertion) operating over minutes to hours at individual synapses, (2) systems consolidation — progressive reorganization of memory traces from hippocampal dependence to neocortical storage over months to years, (3) sleep-dependent reprocessing — offline replay during slow-wave and REM sleep that strengthens consolidated traces. Persistence mechanism: scientific literature, neuroimaging protocols, textbook teaching, and the experimental replication norms of cognitive neuroscience. [formal consolidatio memoriae | substrate: mind | horizon: years | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

An information-theoretic criterion for statistical model selection, defined by the formula AIC = 2k − 2ln(L), where k is the number of estimated parameters in the model and L is the maximized likelihood. The criterion estimates the relative information loss when a given model is used to represent the process that generated the data; lower AIC values indicate less estimated loss. It balances goodness-of-fit (via log-likelihood) against model complexity (via the penalty term 2k), automating the trade-off between underfitting and overfitting. Computed by evaluating each candidate model's log-likelihood at its maximum-likelihood estimates, counting its free parameters, and applying the formula. Published by Hirotugu Akaike in 1974 as derived from Kullback–Leibler divergence, it persists through statistical textbooks, software implementations (R, Python, MATLAB), and research practice across disciplines including econometrics, ecology, signal processing, and machine learning. [formal: AIC | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 2.10]

Sheet music is a human-made document bearing a musical score in standard notation: a page or set of pages whose printed, engraved, or digitally rendered marks — staves, notes, clefs, dynamic and articulation marks, and text — encode a musical work, laid out for a human reader at performance distance. Parameters: (1) notation system — the marks follow the shared syntactic rules of musical notation (staves, clefs, note values, dynamics), without which the page is uninterpretable; (2) part vs. full-score layout — a single instrument or voice part or a complete reduction, with system layout and page turns arranged for a performing reader; (3) format — printed or engraved paper of standard sizes (letter, A4, full-score folio) or a paginated digital rendering of the same layout; (4) reading geometry — orientation, margins, and sizing chosen so a performer can read ahead while playing. Persistence mechanism: produced by typesetting, engraving, printing, or digital typesetting; distributed through music publishers, retail, and licensing; maintained through reprints and successive editions; the form persists as a product category, the designed held-object of the music stand. [formal: folium musicum | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A specification parameter that defines the smallest distinguishable time interval in a measurement or display system. Its value is determined by the sampling rate (for analog-to-digital conversion), frame rate (for visual displays), or refresh rate (for periodic scanning systems). The parameter is set by design choices in the apparatus — bit depth of the time counter, clock frequency of the sampling circuit, or display controller timing — and persists as a fixed specification in the system's documentation and calibration data. [formal: temporal_resolutio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

A butterworth-filter is a human-made filter design — the classic maximally-flat (zero-ripple) magnitude response — defined by its parameters: (1) order N, the number of pole pairs, fixing roll-off beyond cutoff at 20N dB/decade; (2) cutoff frequency wc, where the gain falls to 1/sqrt(2) (-3 dB); (3) the prototype magnitude |H(jw)| = 1/sqrt(1 + (w/wc)^(2N)), whose N poles lie on a left-half s-plane semicircle (for the digital IIR realization, mapped inside the unit circle in the z-plane by the bilinear transform). It persists as the named reference design in every DSP textbook and filter-design toolkit: the standard analog prototype from which digital IIR filters are derived by bilinear transform or impulse invariance, and the flatness yardstick against which Chebyshev and elliptic designs are compared. [formal: filtrum butterworthianum | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.75]

sense-making is a human-constructed cognitive framework through which organisms interpret, organize, and assign meaning to sensory input and experience. Parameters: (1) input — raw data from perception or experience; (2) operation — pattern recognition, categorization, inference, and integration with existing knowledge structures; (3) output — a coherent interpretation or model that reduces uncertainty. Persistence mechanism: the concept persists through cognitive science, psychology, and philosophy as a named construct for a studied cognitive process, taught in academic disciplines, and applied in organizational and clinical practices. [formal: sense-facere | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Violence is a human-made conceptual category that maps the natural act of intentionally inflicting harm on persons, property, or social order. Parameters: (1) agent with intent to harm, (2) target of harm, (3) form of harm (physical, psychological, structural), (4) context of legitimation (legal, moral, ritual). Persistence mechanism: legal codes and penal systems, moral and religious doctrines, narrative and historical accounts, and the institutional practices of conflict resolution and punishment. [formal violentia | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.05]

A barline is the vertical line drawn across a staff that delimits bars (measures): a boundary mark separating one unit of musical time from the next, by which the beat structure set by the time signature is grouped into the recurring segments the eye can navigate. Parameters: (1) position — drawn perpendicular to the staff lines at a bar boundary, spanning the full height of the staff, and in multi-staff systems the same line links every staff of the system so the boundary is visible across parts; (2) kinds — the single thin line at an ordinary bar boundary; the heavier single line closing a section; and the thick-thin final barline closing a piece or a major section; (3) function — the barline is the mark that makes the bar visible: the bar is the unit of musical time the barline delimits, and the two are distinct carvings (the board's accepted definition of bar names the barline as its visual marker). Persistence mechanism: engraved, printed, or digitally rendered as a mark of the score; sustained through the shared conventions of Western staff notation, the engraving and typesetting traditions that place the mark at every boundary, and pedagogy that transmits the convention from score to score and player to player. [formal: linea barica | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Love is the category affective science, philosophy, literature, and ordinary language carve around a complex of attachment, valuation, and care directed toward a person, group, or object. What the map maps: the class of experiences, dispositions, and narratives classified under this name, not a natural substance. Boundaries: (1) against liking — liking is lighter valuation without the commitment and vulnerability component; (2) against infatuation — infatuation is intense attraction without the stable attachment and care dimension; (3) against compassion — compassion is other-directed concern, love adds personal attachment and desire for the other's good as one's own. Persistence: the map persists through the philosophical tradition of friendship and charity, through attachment theory and social psychology research programs, through literary and cultural narratives that codify love's scripts, and through ordinary language that marks love as a distinct relational stance. [formal: amor | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A posterior distribution is the updated probability distribution p(θ|x) over model parameters θ after observing data x, computed by Bayes rule as p(θ|x) proportional to the likelihood p(x|θ) multiplied by the prior distribution p(θ). It encodes the full inferential state of a Bayesian analysis, capturing uncertainty about parameters given observed evidence, and persists as the canonical output of Bayesian computation. [formal: posterior distribution | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Log-likelihood is the natural logarithm of the likelihood function, which evaluates the probability of observed data given a statistical model and its parameters; it is parameterized by the data set, the probability model (including unknown parameters), and persists as a core computational quantity in maximum likelihood estimation, Bayesian inference, hypothesis testing, and model selection criteria. [formal: mathematical | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.60]

backpropagation is a human-made algorithm for computing the gradient of a loss function with respect to all weights in a multi-layer computational graph, most commonly a neural network. It works by applying the chain rule of calculus recursively from the output layer back through each hidden layer, computing local error signals (deltas) at each node and combining them with incoming activations to produce weight gradients. Parameters: network architecture (number and type of layers, activation functions), loss function, computational graph topology. Persistence mechanism: executed as a deterministic computation during each training iteration, producing weight updates via gradient descent or variants. [formal: backpropagation | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A spectrogram is a human-made data visualization that encodes the frequency content of a signal as it varies over time. Its parameters are: (1) frequency axis — the range and resolution of frequency bins (linear or logarithmic scale); (2) time axis — the temporal window and step size of the analysis; (3) amplitude encoding — magnitude representation (linear, decibel, or log scale); (4) window function — the overlap-add kernel (Hamming, Hanning, Blackman) applied per time window. Persistence mechanism: standardized in signal processing toolkits (MATLAB spectrogram, Python scipy.signal.spectrogram, librosa), documented in audio analysis literature, and rendered by audio analysis software for diagnostic and creative use. Distinguished from a frequency spectrum (which shows magnitude vs. frequency at a single moment) by its explicit time dimension, making it a time-frequency representation. [formal: spectrum spectrogram | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A beeswarm plot is a human-made statistical visualization that draws every individual observation as a symbol placed at its true value along a primary axis while offsetting symbols along a perpendicular axis so that no two points overlap, rendering the empirical distribution as a swarm of visible points. Parameters: (1) value axis — the measured quantity on which each point is positioned; (2) grouping axis — the categorical dimension (group, category, or binned continuous variable) along which swarms are aligned; (3) offset algorithm — the rule that spreads points without overlap: ordered packing, force-directed repulsion, or deterministic de-overlapping; (4) scale — number of points per group and number of groups. Persistence mechanism: implemented in statistical graphics libraries (seaborn, ggplot2, matplotlib), embedded in dashboard and exploratory-data-analysis toolchains, and standardized in scientific publication. Distinguished from a histogram by not binning (every observation stays individually visible) and from an ordinary jittered scatter plot by making the offset a non-overlap constraint rather than random noise. [formal: swarm-plot | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

An LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is a signal generator that produces periodic waveforms — typically sine, square, triangle, or sawtooth — at frequencies below the human audible range (conventionally 0.01 Hz to 20 Hz). Unlike audio-rate oscillators, LFOs are not heard directly; instead, they modulate parameters such as pitch (vibrato), amplitude (tremolo), filter cutoff (wah), or delay time (flanging). The output waveform type and modulation rate/frequency determine the character of the effect. Persistence mechanism: circuit implementations in analog synthesizers, lookup-table and numerical algorithms in digital synthesizers and DSP code, documented in electronic music engineering specifications. [formal: lfo | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

sanity-check is a human-made verification routine that applies a quick, coarse test to an artifact or state to confirm it remains within a plausible range before deeper analysis. Parameters: target artifact, invariant or heuristic, check method, threshold for flagging, reporting channel. It persists via codified quick tests, checklists, and institutionalized habits of pausing to verify plausibility. [formal: sanitas probatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

Playful interaction is a human-made pattern of engagement where participants voluntarily enter a bounded frame of low-stakes exploration and feedback, seeking enjoyment rather than instrumental outcome. Parameters: framing (explicit rules or implicit conventions), participant roles, feedback loop speed and clarity, safety framing that permits failure without cost, and repetition tolerance. Persistence is by cultural transmission through demonstration, codified rule sets, media recordings, and institutionalized play spaces that re-enact the frame across generations. The identity log p(x) = ℒ(q) + KL(q(z) || p(z | x)) shows ELBO ≤ log p(x) since KL divergence is non-negative, with equality when q equals the true posterior. It persists as the standard optimization objective in variational inference — maximizing ℒ(q) with respect to q's parameters approximates the posterior while providing a tractable lower bound on model evidence — and is the mathematical foundation of variational autoencoders, implemented in probabilistic programming frameworks (Stan, Pyro, TensorFlow Probability, NumPyro), so that approximate inference remains scalable for models where exact or MCMC inference is intractable.
